look_here_first: Ignore leaf shape at first. Check the upper bracts and then the cyathial gland: E. heterophylla usually has green or only paler-green bracts and a yellow-green gland on a distinct stalk, with a round opening surrounded by an annular rim.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Approved comparison-only taxon; POWO/FNA treat Texas occurrence as introduced/naturalized. Exclude from native metrics.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia: milky latex; the apparent flower is a cyathium with highly reduced male flowers and one central female flower.
morphology_keys.leaves: Highly polymorphic within populations and even on one plant; blades may be lanceolate, elliptic, obovate, pandurate, or lobed. Leaf shape alone is unreliable.
morphology_keys.upper_bracts: Pleiochasial bracts remain green or are only paler green at the base rather than sharply red/pink/white as is typical of E. cyathophora.
morphology_keys.cyathium: One yellow-green gland, stipitate and clavate, about 1–1.4 × 1–1.2 mm; opening circular, occasionally flattened by pressing, with a distinct annular rim; appendages absent.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsule broadly ovoid, about 2.8–3.8 × 4–5.3 mm, three-lobed, usually glabrous and only rarely sparsely puberulent.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds broadly deltoid, about 2.4–2.8 × 1.9–2.4 mm, angular in cross section with a strongly keeled dorsal face and tubercles.
best_field_traits: upper bracts green or merely pale at the base
annular rim present around gland opening
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against E. cyathophora, use the cyathial gland before leaf shape. E. heterophylla = green/pale bracts + stipitate gland + round annular-rimmed opening; E. cyathophora = sharply colored bract bases + sessile/substipitate gland + oblong rimless opening.

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia heterophylla: green or only paler green at base
lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia cyathophora: usually sharply white, pink, or red at base

comparisons.key_distinctions: The strongest field character is the cyathial gland: stipitate + circular opening + annular rim. Bract color is useful supporting evidence; leaf shape is not.
